text: China's cotton-yarn imports are 1,600 kt Jan–Sep 2026 vs 1,040 kt a year earlier. Each tonne is spun abroad from about 1.1 t of lint, so the extra yarn is extra cotton demand in the supplying countries:
items: Vietnam: ~743 kt of yarn to China Jan–Sep (+235 kt y/y) ≈ +258 kt of extra lint (+1.19 m bales), +14% of its 8.3 m-bale USDA import forecast; at the US's usual 34% share that is +0.40 m bales of US cotton (spins imported cotton)
India: ~263 kt of yarn to China Jan–Sep (+173 kt y/y) ≈ +190 kt of extra lint (+0.87 m bales) (spins mostly its own cotton)

Pakistan: ~189 kt of yarn to China Jan–Sep (+41 kt y/y) ≈ +45 kt of extra lint (+0.21 m bales), +4% of its 5.1 m-bale USDA import forecast; at the US's usual 38% share that is +0.08 m bales of US cotton (spins home-grown and imported cotton)
Uzbekistan: ~136 kt of yarn to China Jan–Sep (+27 kt y/y) ≈ +29 kt of extra lint (+0.14 m bales) (spins mostly its own cotton)
Malaysia: ~74 kt of yarn to China Jan–Sep (+12 kt y/y) ≈ +14 kt of extra lint (+0.06 m bales) (spins imported cotton)

Indonesia: ~68 kt of yarn to China Jan–Sep (+47 kt y/y) ≈ +51 kt of extra lint (+0.24 m bales), +11% of its 2.1 m-bale USDA import forecast; at the US's usual 19% share that is +0.05 m bales of US cotton (spins imported cotton)
caveat: These are estimates: this year's country split uses CCFGroup insight 2026-10-23 (China customs HS 5205), 2026-09 for the whole year to date, last year's uses UN Comtrade 2024 (the latest year China has reported to the UN); customs 'cotton yarn' includes blends, so the lint figures are upper bounds. Read it as a tailwind for US and Brazilian sales to Vietnam, Pakistan, Indonesia, not as a revision to the projections.
